speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing agitation and have noticed a yellowish color in your skin and eyes; have you been feeling fatigued, nauseous, or experiencing any pain in your upper right abdomen?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hepatitis B infection (acute).

I note your history of high-risk sexual behavior, which is the primary risk factor here. Given the combination of jaundice, agitation, and social history, we must rule out acute viral hepatitis. I will request the results for Liver Function Tests (LFTs), Hepatitis B Surface Antigen, and Hepatitis C Antibody immediately.
